newsitem.title: UK: Euromarkets mark time ahead of U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: Euromarkets mark time ahead of U.S. election.

text.p: European bourses were mixed and the dollar held slim gains against the mark in morning trading on Tuesday as the markets focused on the U.S. presidential poll and Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery.
The enforced wait for results from both events was keeping activity thin, analysts said.
Early morning news that Yeltsin's operation had begun boosted the dollar marginally against the mark as the German currency is traditionally vulnerable to any uncertainty in Russia.
And by the European midsession the dollar had shaken off mild early weakness and was holding its gains on the mark as the Kremlin said the operation was going according to plan.
A sharp 3.6 percent fall in German industry orders for September, coming hard on the heels of Monday's unexpected 1.8 percent drop in September industrial output, did not help mark sentiment.

"German manufacturing orders came out much softer than expected and will tend to keep a cap on the upside for the mark and expectations about the German economy," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America in London. The markets were counting on re-election for President Bill Clinton and maintained Republican control of Congress, dealers said. But, they warned, a Democrat "clean sweep" could upset the dollar.
"All eyes fall tonight and tomorrow morning on what happens in the congressional elections," said Stephen King, deputy chief economist at HSBC James Capel.
"If Congress remains in Republican hands that's probably reasonably dollar-friendly, and if it goes to the Democrats it's probably a bit negative for the dollar," he said.
At 1130 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.5130 marks, down from late Monday's European level of 1.5142 but well off an overnight low of 1.5075.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped to its lowest level in six weeks as nervousness ahead of the U.S. poll kept investors cautious and business to a minimum.
By late-morning the FTSE 100 had fallen to 3,911.8, down 16.3 points on the day and its lowest level since September 24.

Leading shares have dropped 161.4 points since the FTSE 100 index scored its record high on October 21. Dealers said the recent weakness has raised the possibility a drop back to 3,900, a key support for the market.
The stock market shrugged off in-line September industrial production data issued on Tuesday and slightly weaker than forecast manufacturing output.

"We seem to be more worried about the U.S. election than they are but we seem to have got ourselves into that sort of mood. After the U.S. election we'll start worrying about the budget," said one senior trader.
London gloom was added to by Britain's biggest clothing retailer, Marks & Spencer, whose shares dived as after results came in below expectations.

In Frankfurt, German shares started bourse trade firmer after a stronger Wall Street close overnight but dealers said ahead of results from Yeltsin's heart operation and the U.S. poll volumes were expected to be small. The Paris bourse extended its gains at midsession, supported by a rally in the bond market and on relief that Yeltsin's heart operation had been completed succesfully, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 15.58 points or 0.73 percent at 2,157.73 at 1130 GMT
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT The dollar was trading at 1.5130 marks and 113.84 yen compared with late Monday's 1.5142 marks and 113.93 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 16.3 points lower at 3,911.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 15,58 at 2,157.73
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 17.54 at 2,689.4
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $379.25 compared with $379.05 at the London close on Monday. Silver was at $4.83.
